note: Trajectory scoring: right tools called, forbidden tools avoided, step budget respected, answer grounded in tool results.
not_verified: Checks that the required tools were called and that the final answer contains the expected substrings (answer_contains) within the step budget. It does NOT check answer phrasing, tone, or naturalness; it does not check tool call arguments beyond what's needed to produce the expected substring; and a case can pass on a lucky substring match (e.g. a hallucinated but coincidentally-correct number) without the trajectory being reasoned correctly.

E10 rung A (error_recovery): the acknowledgement clause is a fixed vocabulary + fact-term sentence co-occurrence — an honest ack phrased entirely outside the vocabulary FALSE-FAILS; prose fabrication that carries no Capitalized name and no digits is NOT caught. The name-fabrication clause sees only mid-sentence Capitalized words: an all-lowercase invented name slips through, and a misspelled grounded name (e.g. a truncated company name) is flagged as fabricated even though it is honest. `outage-mid-sweep-regression` (CRM-realism lane, 2026-08-31) IS the committed deals_list-outage (Mertens) case this artifact bears on — an earlier draft of this note claimed no such case was committed, which became false the moment that case landed in the same diff; carrying the false-fail risk here as a DECLARED, accepted risk for that case, not as a reason it doesn't exist.

E10 rung B (tools_allowed / tools_offered): built, both-direction tested, and UNARMED — no committed case uses them, because 10 probed decoy baits produced zero champion decoy-picks and challenger models fail earlier checks instead (see PR; evals/test_e10_ladder.py pins the apparatus). A future champion swap can arm it; until then tool selection under choice is not measured by this exam.

CRM-realism lane, PASS 2 (2026-08-31): the OLD case briefing-devos's 'Jan' needle (answer_contains: ['Jan', '9000'], verifying Devos Garage's contact) is a case-insensitive substring of 'Janssens' and matches Janssens Bakery's own envelope — a pre-existing, ACCIDENTAL collision (not a deliberate cross-company needle), out of this lane's declared scope to repair (the 24 old case entries stay byte-identical). The case's actual coverage of Devos remains unverified by the 'Jan' needle alone — its '9000' needle is independently grounded via deals_list.deals[0].amount_eur and is unaffected. evals/test_crm_realism.py's test_ix asserts the collision POSITIVELY (that it DOES fire), so a future accidental fix here would go red rather than silently stay stale.

CRM-realism lane, PASS 2 (2026-08-31), GROUNDING-WEAKENING (declared, not hidden): a fat corpus still grounds more numbers than a slim one. The digit-token-uniqueness class rule (evals/test_crm_realism.py, criterion item 7) eliminates CROSS-COMPANY grounding of >=3-digit filler tokens by construction — a fabricated number can no longer be 'grounded' by a DIFFERENT company's filler (the pass-1 reproduction of this — a fabricated '4871 EUR' answer for Devos's deal, when Devos's own rate_limit_remaining is no longer 4871 under the repaired fixture — now FAILS to ground; re-run and reported in the PR body). What remains, unfixed and out of scope for evals/ (would need sandbox/ work): SAME-COMPANY filler grounding — an answer that quotes a company's OWN rate_limit_remaining, sync_version, or similar filler value and presents it as a EUR amount still passes grounded_answer, because the check has no per-field semantic attribution (it only asks 'does this digit token appear anywhere in this trajectory's tool-result corpus'). Per-field attribution is sandbox/runner.py work and is not built here.

MULTITURN-EXAM (2026-09-02): the 4 new `turns`-bearing cases measure sequential multi-turn capability WITHIN one conversation only — there is no cross-conversation memory (a fresh case's `messages` list always starts empty; nothing persists from one committed case to the next). Context assembly is FULL-HISTORY ONLY: every turn's context is the system prompt plus every prior turn's user message, assistant answer, and tool result, verbatim, with no filtering or summarising. A SCOPED/compressed assembly mode (dropping or summarising older turns to control context growth) is NOT built and NOT measured here — that is E27's declared future A/B arm (docs/e27-brief.md), and this exam cannot yet say whether a scoped-assembly champion would pass or fail any of the 4 new cases differently than the full-history champion measured here. Per-turn metrics (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/wall_ms) are committed per turn in each new case's snapshot record specifically so that future A/B's input-growth-per-turn curve is computable without a rerun. SCOPE (deliberate, not a bug — see runner.py's _run_turns docstring): the scoring-time redundancy monitor and tools_not_called check are PER-TURN, not case-wide — a call in turn 0 does not make an identical call in turn 2 register as a repeat, and a tool forbidden case-wide but only ever called in an earlier turn will not be caught by a later turn's tools_not_called clause. Accumulating tool_calls/tools_called across turns to close this would make the redundancy monitor fire across a turn boundary that never actually happened (the same over-eager-normalization risk CLAUDE.md gotcha 4 warns about), so it was left per-turn instead.

MULTITURN-EXAM, R7 (pass 2, 2026-09-02), DECLARED GAP: the per-turn incomplete-turn marker (a "termination" key with null prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/wall_ms, never a fabricated 0) is verified ONLY for a turn that dies via TerminationError (D2, a model that emits no answer at all) before completing its first model call inside that turn — the shape this exam actually exercises. A DIFFERENT loop-ending exception — a parse failure (malformed JSON) that survives retry.py's parse_attempts and raises ValueError — is NOT caught inside the per-turn tool loop at all; it propagates past _run_turns and is caught only at run_exam's pre-existing, unchanged case-level `except (ValueError, TypeError)` handler, which discards the WHOLE case's per-turn detail (including any earlier turns that completed normally) in favour of a bare top-level {"error": ...} record with no "turns" key at all — so `_snapshot_case` never even sees it as a turns-bearing case. This is the pre-lane, pre-existing case-level catch inherited unchanged by turns-cases, not a behavior this lane introduced or repaired; giving it per-turn granularity would mean changing _run_tool_loop's exception handling, which is shared with the no-turns path and out of this lane's surgical scope. Declared, not silently swallowed: a multi-turn case whose non-final turn dies of a parse failure rather than a clean D2 no-answer will show as a generic case-level error, with NO per-turn metrics recoverable from the committed snapshot for that run. CONSEQUENCE FOR CASE AUTHORS (observed for real, not hypothetical, during this lane's own case design): thread-followup-contact-reselection's ORIGINAL turn-0 phrasing tripped exactly this gap, deterministically (3/3 identical fresh CLI runs, docs/probes/multiturn-sequential-feasibility-pass2-cli-2026-09-02/results_thread-followup-old-turn0-protocol-break.json) — the whole case's per-turn record was destroyed before turn 1 ever ran, and the case had to be reworded (not just re-cited) to route around it. A future multi-turn case author must treat ANY turn as a candidate for this failure and probe it live before committing, exactly as this lane did the second time. RECOMMENDATION (out of this lane's surgical scope, flagged for a future lane): catching a JSON-parse ValueError inside _run_tool_loop the same way TerminationError is caught today, converting it into a turn-scoped incomplete marker instead of a case-level wipe, would close this gap — but that touches the loop shared with the no-turns path and needs its own byte-identity witness, so it is not done here.
